added.name: Reific
added.long_description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. Each comes from real, de-identified records (health data, industrial sensors, compute-cluster logs), in three families: personal agents, industry, and science and compute. The world keeps moving while the agent works, so the agent must keep learning: data arrive on a clock, and every answer is checked against what actually happened. In each family, the best frontier model averages below half, and models that train on our environments improve.

We specialise in time series because almost everything that matters is recorded that way: a heartbeat, a power grid, a factory line, a GPU cluster, an experiment. No person can turn thousands of moving signals at once into the state of a system and what happens next. AI can pass the bar exam, but it still can’t watch a system for weeks and act at the right moment. It learned from what people wrote down, in environments that freeze the world and abstract it to our understanding.

Time series let us ride the exponential. The world records new data every second and time keeps grading, so each generation of models gets harder, fresher tasks. We believe humans always strive to explore. Our mission is to build the infrastructure for that exploration: the layer of the AI stack where models keep improving, out into what no one understands yet.
added.one_liner: RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time

long_description.before:
Ranla is an AI growth marketer for PLG SaaS teams. You instrument product events once; Ranla segments users, plans lifecycle campaigns, writes the email, sends it on infrastructure you control, and reports back in dollars — trials converted, upgrades, churn risk — not just opens and clicks.

Most founders ship the product but never hire a lifecycle marketer. Ranla owns that loop: weekly plans, occasion-based sends, A/B tests, and approval flows so nothing goes out without you when you want a gate. Transactional and lifecycle email live on the same stack, so password resets and onboarding drips aren't split across Resend plus a separate ESP.

We're built for teams with signups and revenue data but no one running email full time — the gap between "we have users" and "we have a growth motion."

long_description.before:
CatchAll by NewsCatcher is a recall-first web search API built for queries where the results are spread across hundreds or thousands of pages on the web. Instead of returning the top ranked links like traditional search engines, CatchAll retrieves a large candidate set from the web, validates which pages actually match the query, and extracts structured records of real-world events.

Developers and data teams use CatchAll to answer “long-list” questions such as tracking regulatory actions, funding rounds, product launches, corporate expansions, or cybersecurity incidents. The output is not just links but clean, deduplicated datasets that can power AI agents, monitoring systems, analytics pipelines, and market intelligence workflows.

CatchAll runs on the data infrastructure developed by NewsCatcher, which continuously indexes millions of articles and public web pages across a global network of sources.
long_description.after:
NewsCatcher turns global news and web coverage into structured, ready-to-use data. We index 140,000+ sources in 50+ languages, so teams can monitor any company, market, topic or real-world event continuously, and act on it before it reaches them elsewhere.

Two ways in, on one key. The News API returns ranked articles in any language, grouped into stories so repeated coverage of one event arrives as one event, plus boolean search across the last 12 months when you need every match rather than the best ones. The Agent handles the questions no single page answers like every funding round, regulatory action, product launch or cybersecurity incident in a window, or the news about every company on a list. It retrieves a large candidate set from the web, validates which pages actually match, and returns a table with a source on every row.

long_description.before: Cardinal Square is building AI-native schools, starting unaccredited with an after-school writing class before building full, accredited schools. We think education is going to look very different in a few years; not a world without teachers, but one where great educators and AI work side by side to deliver personalized education to every student.
long_description.after:
First, we build AI teachers that read every step of a kid’s work, remember how that kid learns, and adapt to them every day. Our goal is an AI that teaches as well as the best human tutor.

Then we take the programs families already pay hundreds a month for (tutoring centers, writing schools, daily practice programs) and rebuild them around our AI teacher, so every family gets personalized education for a fraction of the price. It’s the same ritual families trust from Kumon or a writing school, with the AI teacher doing the teaching.

long_description.before:
ChampionEffect is an AI Coach that teaches AI to every employee at a company, in Slack and Teams.

Coach helps with a new AI concept, a new workflow or any tool. It jumps on a call and walks you through the work, just like a coworker would. It points to the top use cases in your industry and tailors everything to your company’s needs and tools. Every time someone does a walkthrough with Coach, it learns from it and suggests a better way to the next coworker.

Before this, we ran a YC company (Cambly) that taught English to millions of professionals and generated $100M+ in revenue. Now we’re using what we learned to teach millions about AI.
